source.note: Readings for the terms whose romaji in this repository does not pin down the pronunciation, almost always because it does not mark a long vowel: the romaji "Dojo" is どじょ or どうじょう and cannot say which. Kana is what the audio scripts use. IPA and pitch accent are for the human voice brief: neither synthesiser can be told an accent, and accent is exactly what separates ko-uchi from kōchi, so it is the one thing a recorded voice can give that a generated one cannot. `derived` marks a reading worked out from the romaji plus a confirmed component rather than looked up whole; `looked-up` marks one taken from the entry named.

readings.note: This book writes Sempai, the older Hepburn spelling of ん before a labial. The kana is せんぱい either way.
Written Shimpan here for the same reason as Sempai.
